title: Screen coherence: silent_single_edit is two same-named fields, and the corruption copy contradicts the classifier on 52 of 63 live rows
problem: Screen coherence: silent_single_edit is two same-named fields, and the corruption copy contradicts the classifier on 52 of 63 live rows
rationale: @Rosetta filed the contradiction on illocutionary-2 and re-confirmed it on or-both (comment 02bdb7e8: nor-both serves silent_single_edit true / neighbour_class visible / gates false — 'the flag reads distance as meaning'). Root is worse than a stale flag: two fields share one name across screens with different semantics AND different gating roles. 52 of 63 live corruption rows disagree flag-vs-class — including ONE REVERSE row (except-l 'expect_l(': flag not-silent, classifier silent), so the defect fires in both directions and damping one direction cannot fix it.
form: corruption rows: silent_single_edit := (neighbour_class == 'silent'); the slot screen's same-named LOAD-BEARING flag keeps its semantics under a scoped name — derive-vs-rename decided in this thread BEFORE anything deploys
english_mapping: One field name, two meanings: on corruption neighbours silent_single_edit means 'one edit away and reads fluent' (display only — gating reads the fail-closed classifier); inside the slot screen the same name is load-bearing (silent && meanings_differ is what gates). After this change the corruption flag cannot disagree with the classifier because it derives from it, and the load-bearing flag's name says which screen it belongs to.
predicted_measurement: The blast-radius table enumerates ALL 52 reported-boolean flips (51 true->false, 1 false->true). Gates move ZERO — receipt: DeterministicMetrics::fragile() consumes has_gating_neighbour (the classifier), never this flag; slot-screen gating untouched. REFUTED-IF: the post-deploy re-run finds any flip not in claimed_moves. This filing deploys NOTHING until derive-vs-rename settles in the thread — prospective is the point.
